keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Multan row; its Sind-Habbari Dynasty row, 229,898 km2, covers the Mansura emirate to the south). The page calls the principality "located in southern Punjab", says it bordered "the Hindu Shahi kingdom in northern Punjab" and the "Habbari Emirate" to the south, and gives no area. The 120 km radius round Multan is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the emirate "located in southern Punjab", centred on Multan

ledger.note: 855: the Banu Munabbih take Multan. "Multan also became capital of an independent emirate under an Arab tribe, the Banū Munabbih (855-959)"; infobox "Munabbih I came to power under Abbasid Caliphate: 855" and independence declared in 861 "Anarchy at Samarra".

959: the Ismaili / Qarmatian dynasty replaces the Banu Munabbih. Jalam ibn Shayban, a Fatimid da'i, "had overthrown the Banu Munabbih in 959"; infobox "Banu Lawi overthrew the Banu Munabbih: 959". The state and colour continue.

region.text: the emirate "located in southern Punjab", centred on Multan

ledger.note: 1006: Mahmud of Ghazni marches on Multan. "Mahmud marched against Multan in 1006 CE due to its Ismaili element and Daud turning against him." The Fateh Daud page records an annual tribute of 200,000 golden dirhams and a conversion to Sunni Hanafi fiqh after his submission (undated); the Ghaznavid dossier should carry the tribute as vassal_start.

region.text: the emirate "located in southern Punjab", centred on Multan

ledger.note: 1010: the Ghaznavids conquer Multan. "In 1010, Daud again rebelled against Mahmud, who marched on the city during his eighth invasion of India"; Daud "was defeated and imprisoned at the fort of Ghurak, situated between Ghazni and Lamghan, for the rest of his life".

region.text: the emirate "located in southern Punjab", centred on Multan

ledger.note: 1010: Multan passes to the Ghaznavids. Infobox "Ghaznavid conquest of Multan: 1010".

region.text: the emirate "located in southern Punjab", centred on Multan

ledger.note: 1010: the Emirate of Multan ends. Isma'ilism "survived in Multan and later in Sindh, where Soomra emirs gave them protection"; the page mentions an Ismaili rebellion in 1041 and nothing on Ghurid rule or 1175.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Multan

zones.text: the emirate "located in southern Punjab", centred on Multan

wars.outcome: Mahmud marched on Multan in 1006 because of its Isma'ili element and Daud's defection, and again in 1010 during his eighth invasion of India; Daud was imprisoned at Ghurak and Multan annexed.
wars.note: Anandapala's page (Hindu Shahis dossier) puts Anandapala's refusal of passage to Multan in 1006. Firishta (cited on this page) has Jayapala ceding Lamghan and Multan to Hamid in an alliance, which the Hindu Shahi page does not support.

certainty.note: No frontier is given on any page; the radius round Multan is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no Multan row. Two pages; neither gives an area or a frontier. The dossier ends in 1010 because the emirate page does; the later Ismaili rebellions (1041, Rajpal ibn Sumar) are not dated on the pages and a Multan principality up to 1175-1176 (the brief's suggestion) is not supported. The Ghaznavid Empire dossier should carry a vassal_start for 1006 (counterpart emirate-of-multan) if it follows the page. Gazetteer note: 'Multan' is a place; no change needed.
